206.description: The part of the file the `Range` asked for

get.summary:
The folders every other is within: on Windows, the root of each drive with a letter, `C:\`,
mapped network drives among them; elsewhere, `/` alone.

parameters.name: edit
parameters.description: Read up to 10 MiB, to edit, rather than 2 MiB.

put.summary:
Saves text as a file: over it only if it is still at the `version` it was read at, or as a new
file. One changed since is refused with 409 and the problem type `changed`; one deleted since,
with 404.

409.description: A file of that name is there

post.summary:
Changes to folders, as an event stream: a `change` event, its data the folder as asked for,
whenever what that holds may have changed, at most about once a second for each, after which it
is to be listed again. A folder that is not there, or goes away, is told of by a `gone` event,
and one that cannot be watched, or is no path, by an `unwatched` event; the others are followed
on. Events missed while the stream was not open are not told, so the folders are listed again on
reconnecting. One stream follows many folders: a browser holds few connections to a server.

parameters.name: path
parameters.description: The folder, for all it holds.

parameters.name: selection
parameters.description: The id `POST /api/files/zip/selection` gave the entries chosen, for just those.

post.summary:
Keeps entries chosen for a zip of them, under the folder they are all in, which
`GET /api/files/zip` then downloads by the id given: their names would make too long an
address.

get.summary:
What the commit changed from its first parent, or from nothing for a first commit: each file
with the lines it added and removed, and the commit's whole message.

parameters.name: repo
parameters.description: The repository's folder, as a listing names it.

post.summary:
Commits what is staged, as from a terminal: the repository's hooks run, and the commit is
signed if the user's config says so. git runs to its end, however long its hooks take; past five
minutes the answer is a problem saying so. What a hook or git says when it fails is the
problem's detail.

get.summary:
The lines each change since the last commit of the repository whose folder is `repo` adds and
removes, staged or not, new files' too. A binary file's, or one past 10 MiB, are not counted.
Read by running git, which runs no program the repository's own config names.

The file `path` as the commit `commit` of the repository whose folder is `repo` holds it, to
compare with what is on disk: its text, up to 10 MiB. A path the commit holds no file at, or a
folder, a symlink or a submodule, is 404 with the problem type `not-committed`. Read by running
git, which reads only its own objects and fetches none.

parameters.name: repo
parameters.description: The repository's folder, as a listing names it.

parameters.name: commit
parameters.description: The commit's full id, as the repository's status names it.

parameters.name: path
parameters.description: Where the file is in the repository, its names separated by `/`, as a change names it.

get.summary: The commits from `head` back, newest first, 50 at a time.

parameters.name: repo
parameters.description: The repository's folder, as a listing names it.

parameters.name: head
parameters.description:
The commit the history goes back from, by its full id, as the repository's status names
it: the same for every page.

parameters.name: skip
parameters.description: How many commits the pages before this one held.

post.summary:
Stages what changed at `paths`, new and deleted files too, as `git add -A` does: with the
filters the repository names, as from a terminal.

get.summary:
How the repository whose folder is `repo` stands: its branch, and the entries changed, new or
ignored since its last commit. Read again for each request, by running git, which runs no
program the repository's own config names.

post.summary: Unstages `paths`: the index takes them back as the last commit holds them.

204.description: The push service took the notification

410.description: The push service no longer knows this device

parameters.name: session
parameters.description: Only those of this Meka session.

400.description: The folder is not one, or too many terminals are open

Change.description: An entry that differs from the last commit, or that git ignores.

path.description:
Where it is in the repository, its names separated by `/`. A folder git tells of as a
whole, new or ignored with all it holds, ends with `/`.

submodule.description:
Whether it is a submodule, changed as its commit did; what changed inside it is its own
status's to tell.

ChangeKind.description: How an entry differs from the last commit, as Files marks it.

ChangedFile.description:
A file a commit changed, with the lines it added and removed: none for a binary file, or one
past 10 MiB.

path.description: Where it is in the repository after the commit, its names separated by `/`.

Commit.description: A commit, as the history lists it.

date.description: When its author wrote it, in RFC 3339.

parents.description: The commits it follows: none for a first commit, two or more for a merge.

CommitChanges.description: What a commit changed from the commit before it: its first parent, for a merge.

date.description: When its author wrote it, in RFC 3339.

too_many.description: Whether more changed than are told: past 10,000, none are.

CommittedFile.description: A file as a commit holds it, to compare with what is on disk.

binary.description: Whether it looks binary, in which case `text` is empty.

too_large.description: Whether it is past 10 MiB, the most the editor takes, in which case `text` is empty.

Confirmation.description: Confirming who you are: a passkey's answer, or the password where there is no passkey.

Confirmed.description: When the person confirmed who they are.

DesktopSettings.description: The desktop app's settings. One missing from the saved settings takes its default.

check_updates.description: Whether GitHub is asked once a day for a newer release.

notifications.description: Whether system notifications are shown: of turns, downloads and newer releases.

logs.description: The folder Meka's log is written to.

portable.description: Whether the app is a portable copy, keeping everything in a folder beside it.

oneOf.description: A newer release of Meka Studio, if the last check found one.

current.description: Whether it is the device asking.

device.description: Its browser and system, with their versions, from its user agent.

name.description: What it is called: its own name, or one from its browser.

DiffStat.description: The lines each change since the last commit adds and removes.

files.description: Each file changed, new ones too, by its path as the status names it.

too_many.description: Whether more changed than are told: past 10,000, none are.

hidden.description: Whether its name starts with a dot, or the system marks it hidden.

permissions.description: Its permissions, as `ls` writes them: `rwxr-xr-x`. Windows has none.

size.description: Its size in bytes; a folder's is what the file system says of it.

target.description: Where a symlink points, as written.

oneOf.description: What a symlink leads to, if anything.

push.description: Whether push notifications can be sent.

FileStat.description: The lines a file's change adds and removes: none for a binary file, or one past 10 MiB.

replace.description: Whether to replace a file of the same name.

Folder.description: A folder of the desktop app's that the interface can open in the file manager.

ahead.description:
How many commits it has that its upstream does not, and the other way around; none where
the upstream is not there.

branch.description: The branch checked out; none when a commit is checked out on its own.

commit.description: The commit checked out; none before the first.

git_dir.description: Its git folder, absolute, which staging, committing and switching branches change.

too_many.description: Whether more changed than are told: past 10,000, none are.

upstream.description: The branch it follows, if any.

History.description: A page of a branch's history, newest first.

home.description: The home folder, absolute, which `~` names; none where it is not known.

repo.description:
The folder of the git repository the folder is in, absolute; none where it is in none, or
git is not installed.

device.description: The device, named from its browser.

MekaProcess.description: The Meka the desktop app runs.

last_exit.description: How it last ended, such as "exit status: 1", if it has.

pid.description: Its process id, while it runs.

error.description: Why the last check failed, when it did.

reachable.description: Whether Meka answered the last check.

supported.description: Whether that version is one this release works with.

verified.description: Whether that version is one this release was checked against.

repo.description: The repository's folder, as a listing names it.

tracked.description: Stage every change to a file git already tracks first, as `git commit -a` does.

parents.description: Whether to make any folders above it that are missing too.

NewPasskey.description: A new passkey: the authenticator's answer and what to call it.

NewPassword.description: A new password, and the one it replaces.

NewSelection.description: Entries chosen, to download as one zip under the folder they are all in.

cwd.description: The folder to start in; the home folder unless given.

session.description: The Meka session it belongs to, if any: it is found by it, and closes with it.

replace.description: Whether it may replace a file of the same name, when it finishes.

PasskeyAnswer.description: A passkey's answer to a challenge.

credential.description: The credential the browser returned, with its bytes in URL-safe base64.

PasskeyChallenge.description: A challenge for the browser to put to an authenticator.

id.description: The id the answer comes back with.

options.description: The options for `navigator.credentials`, with their bytes in URL-safe base64.

Paths.description: Paths in a repository to stage or unstage.

paths.description:
Each a path in the repository, its names separated by `/`, or a folder in it, taken as
written; `.` is the whole repository.

repo.description: The repository's folder, as a listing names it.

Preferences.description: The preferences every device shares, as the interface writes them.

Problem.description: A problem, as the API answers it.

title.description: The kind of problem, in words.

type.description: `urn:meka-studio:` and what kind of problem it is.

PushState.description: Whether push notifications work, and whether this device receives them.

enabled.description: Whether Meka Studio can send them.

endpoint.description: The endpoint this device subscribed with, to tell whether the browser's is the same.

public_key.description: The key to subscribe with, uncompressed, in URL-safe base64.

name.description: The name; empty goes back to the default.

SaveText.description: Text to save as a file.

version.description:
The version the file was read at, which it must still be at; none to make a new file,
never over anything there.
What it holds now, to save over it next.

SelectionMade.description: The id a selection's zip downloads by.

SessionView.description: Who is signed in, on which device, and what they can confirm themselves with.

desktop.description:
Whether this is the desktop app's window, which signs itself in and has no password,
passkeys, other devices or push notifications to manage.

device_id.description: This sign-in's id, as the devices list names it.

fresh_seconds.description: How long a confirmation counts for a risky change, in seconds.

has_passkeys.description: Whether the user has a passkey.

passkeys_available.description: Whether passkeys work at this address.

verified_at.description: When the person last confirmed who they are on this device.

SignedOut.description: How many devices were signed out.

Staged.description: How much of an entry's change is staged, to be committed next.

StatusView.description: How Meka Studio and Meka stand.

meka.description: How Meka stood at the last check.

versions.description: The Meka versions this release supports.

Subscription.description: A browser's push subscription, as `PushSubscription.toJSON()` writes it.

TerminalView.description: A terminal, as the list shows it.

active_at.description: When it was last typed in, attached to or left.

session.description: The Meka session it belongs to, if any.

Text.description: A text file's contents, for a preview or to edit.

binary.description: Whether the file looks binary, in which case `text` is empty.

truncated.description: Whether the file is longer than what was read.

version.description: What the file held, to save over it only as it was: none for one cut short or binary.

Update.description: A newer release of Meka Studio.

chunk_bytes.description: The most bytes a piece may hold.

Versions.description: The Meka versions this release supports.

minimum.description: The oldest Meka it works with.

verified.description: The versions it was checked against.

paths.description: Each folder, at most 64, as the events name it.

ZoomStep.description: A step of the window's zoom.

Zooming.description: How the window's zoom is to change.
